items.title: Glucagon Explained: The Peptide Behind Retatrutide’s Secret Weapon
items.summary: What if one of the most important peptides in your body does almost the OPPOSITE of insulin? It's called glucagon. Insulin helps lower blood sugar. Glucagon can help raise it — and it's so powerful that glucagon is used as an emergency medicine for severe low blood sugar. But that's only part of the story. Scientists are now targeting the glucagon system alongside GLP-1 and GIP in retatrutide, an experimental triple-receptor agonist producing remarkable results in human trials. In this video, we break down: What glucagon is and how it works Why glucagon can raise blood sugar How glucagon differs from insulin Why glucagon is an established medicine Why scientists would target glucagon for weight loss How retatrutide targets GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon The human evidence behind retatrutide Why “glucagon is the opposite of insulin” is useful — but an oversimplification In a Phase 2 trial, the highest retatrutide dose produced 24.2% average weight loss at 48 weeks. More recently, Lilly reported 28.3% average weight loss at 80 weeks at the highest dose in its Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 trial. Retatrutide remains investigational and is not currently FDA approved. 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research. Education. items.title: Thymosin Alpha-1 may be one of the most studied peptides you’ve never heard of.
items.summary: While many popular peptides have limited human evidence, Thymosin Alpha-1 has been investigated across 30+ clinical studies involving more than 11,000 human subjects. Researchers have explored its effects on the immune system, serious infections, cancer, and other immune-related conditions. But one of the largest trials produced a surprising result. In this video, we break down: 🔬 What Thymosin Alpha-1 actually is 🛡️ Why it's called an “immune peptide” 👥 The research involving 11,000+ human subjects 📊 What earlier studies appeared to show ⚠️ What happened in a 1,106-person Phase 3 sepsis trial 🧬 What the human evidence actually tells us Is Thymosin Alpha-1 really an immune peptide — or have the claims gotten ahead of the evidence? items.title: Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
items.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. items.title: Gut Doctor: Stop Fibermaxxing! Eat These 3 Foods Instead
items.summary: Dr. Karan Rajan on Fiber Fermentation, Sodium Myths, and What Your Poop Reveals About Disease Risk Your poop is more predictive than almost any other health signal, and you are flushing that data away every single day without a second look. Host Dave Asprey sits down with Dr. Karan Rajan, a practicing NHS gastrointestinal surgeon, best-selling author, and Chief Science Officer at Throne, who has built a following of over 12 million people by making gut science accessible and actionable. He has spent his career removing colon cancers, treating digestive disease, and now studies how gut bacteria drive nearly every system in the body, from hormone metabolism to brain optimization. They break down why fibermaxxing can backfire without the right mix of fast, medium, and slow fermenting fibers, and why generic "eat more fiber" advice ignores what your gut bacteria actually need. The conversation covers protein absorption limits and how much your body can really use, the truth about saturated fat and metabolism, and why the sodium-to-potassium ratio matters more than sodium alone. They also dig into fasting and the gut's natural cleaning cycle, the estrobolome and testobolome and their role in hormone balance and longevity, and how AI is starting to reshape personalized health data, supplements, and functional medicine. items.title: The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk
items.summary: Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. This is a perfect example of why the question isn't simply “Do peptides work?” The better question is: Which peptide, for what purpose, and where is the human evidence? 📘 FREE Peptide Guide: PeptideAtoZ.com/free-guide 💬 Join the Peptide A to Z Community: PeptideAtoZ.com/community 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research.
